seo.title: Zell am See ski resort guide
seo.description: 77 km of pistes above a lakeside town - 30 km blue, 28 km red, 19 km black - served by 27 lifts, with the season opening 4 December 2026.

h1: Zell am See ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Zell am See sits on the shore of its lake at 764 metres, with the Schmittenhöhe rising straight out of the town. The mountain holds 77 kilometres of pistes - 30 blue, 28 red and 19 black - served by 27 lift facilities, six of them express lifts that feed the area from Schüttdorf, Zell am See and Viehhofen. Five valley runs each drop more than a thousand vertical metres back to the lake.
stayOverview: The town is on the lake, with the Schmittenhöhebahn and the cityXpress leaving from its edge. Schüttdorf is the quieter end, served by the areitXpress, and Viehhofen is over the shoulder of the mountain on the zellamseeXpress.
hotelIntro: Book against high season. The town puts you by the lake and within reach of two lifts; Schüttdorf is cheaper and has its own gondola.
rentalCars: Zell am See is on the Pinzgau railway and about 80 kilometres south of Salzburg, with the Grossglockner road closed in winter.

verticalDrop.unannounced: The operator states that five long valley runs each have more than 1,000 vertical metres, but publishes no vertical drop for the ski area itself.

topElevation.unannounced: No summit elevation is published for the ski area on the skiing, winter, highlights or season pages. The altitudes the operator gives - 1,765 m at Hochmais, 1,715 m at the snowpark - are for named features, not the top of the lift system.

baseElevation.unannounced: The lift company's skiing pages give the piste kilometres, their split by grade and the lift count, and mention five valley runs of more than 1,000 vertical metres, but state no valley-station altitude.

longestRun.unannounced: The lift company names five long valley runs of more than 1,000 vertical metres each, but does not say which is longest or how long any of them is.

dayPass.note: The Ski ALPIN CARD day ticket in the peak period, 19 December 2026 to 12 March 2027. It is EUR 74.00 from 27 November to 18 December 2026 and from 13 March to 4 April 2027.

facts.text: 30 of the 77 piste kilometres are graded easy, and the children’s areas are built around Schmidolin, the Schmitten dragon.
19 km of black runs, eight marked ski routes for off-piste, and five valley runs with more than 1,000 vertical metres each.
The Snowpark at 1,715 m splits into a beginner and an advanced area, and the Funslope XXL runs over a kilometre from 1,765 m.
